questions.stem: Which of these statements is <u>wrong</u> about the location of Eritrea?

options.A: Eritrea is found north of the equator.
options.B: Eritrea is found to the west of the Red Sea.
options.C: Eritrea is found to the east of Sudan.
options.D: Eritrea has no border with Djibouti.

explanation_steps: Eritrea is north of the equator (between about 12°N and 18°N). So A is true.
Eritrea is on the western shore of the Red Sea. So B is true.
Sudan is to the west of Eritrea, so Eritrea is east of Sudan. C is true.
The textbook says Eritrea is bordered by Djibouti in the south-east (Social Studies Grade 6, p. 23). So D is wrong. Answer: D.
questions.explain_simple: Eritrea has a border with Djibouti. So statement D is wrong.
tips: Neighbours of Eritrea: Sudan, Ethiopia, Djibouti. The Red Sea is to the east.

similar_questions.stem: Which country is found to the south-east of Eritrea?
explanation_steps: Djibouti borders Eritrea in the south-east. Answer: B.

questions.stem: The queen who sent ships to the Land of Punt in 1500 B.C.E was:
explanation_steps: The textbook says: in 1500 B.C. Queen Hatshepsut of Egypt sent ships to the Land of Punt (Social Studies Grade 6, p. 60).
Answer: B.
questions.explain_simple: Queen Hatshepsut of Egypt sent ships to Punt.
tips: Punt + Egypt + ships = Hatshepsut.

similar_questions.stem: From which country did Queen Hatshepsut send ships to Punt?
explanation_steps: Hatshepsut was a queen of Egypt. Answer: A.

questions.stem: The lowest stage in human development is called
explanation_steps: Human society developed from lower to higher stages: primitive communal, then slave society, then feudal society (Social Studies Grade 7, Unit 5).
The first and lowest stage is the primitive communal society. Answer: B.
questions.explain_simple: The first (lowest) stage is primitive communal society.
tips: Order: primitive communal → slave → feudal → capitalist.

similar_questions.stem: Which society came after the primitive communal society?
explanation_steps: Slave society came second. Answer: B.

questions.stem: Volcanoes have _____ stages in their life cycle.
explanation_steps: The textbook says: volcanic mountains pass through three stages in their life cycle (Social Studies Grade 7, p. 120).
The three stages are active, dormant (sleeping) and extinct (dead). Answer: B.
questions.explain_simple: A volcano has three stages: active, dormant and extinct.
tips: Active (erupting) → dormant (sleeping) → extinct (dead).

similar_questions.stem: A volcano that will never erupt again is called:
explanation_steps: A dead volcano is extinct. Answer: C.

questions.stem: Relief describes the:

options.B: vegetation cover of the earth’s surface
options.D: the rocks of the earth’s surface

explanation_steps: Relief means the shape of the land: mountains, plateaus, valleys and plains (Social Studies Grade 8, p. 2).
It is not climate, plants or rocks. Answer: C.
questions.explain_simple: Relief is the shape of the land.
tips: Relief = high and low land (mountains, plains, valleys).

similar_questions.stem: Which of these is a relief feature?
explanation_steps: A plateau is a shape of the land. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Social Studies Grade 8 textbook – Unit 1 – Relief in Eritrea, 1.1 What is Relief?, p. 2

questions.stem: In Eritrea, which of these rivers has different direction from the others?
explanation_steps: Mereb, Barka and Anseba start in the highlands and flow west or north-west into the Sudan (Social Studies Grade 8, p. 16).
The Haddas starts near Adi Keih, cuts through the Eastern Escarpment and goes to the Red Sea (Social Studies Grade 8, p. 17). Answer: A.
questions.explain_simple: The Haddas goes to the Red Sea. The others go west to Sudan.
tips: Learn the rivers by the sea they go to: Red Sea rivers (Haddas, Laba, Wekiro) and western rivers (Mereb, Barka, Anseba, Setit).

similar_questions.stem: Which river flows into the Red Sea?
explanation_steps: The Felket enters the Red Sea at Mersa Teklay. Answer: C.

questions.stem: Eritrea is located between latitudes of _________ and ________.
explanation_steps: The textbook says Eritrea is located between 12°N and 18°N latitudes (Social Studies Grade 8, p. 54).
36°E and 43°E are its longitudes, not latitudes. Answer: B.
questions.explain_simple: Eritrea is between 12°N and 18°N.
tips: Latitude = N or S (12°N–18°N). Longitude = E or W (36°E–43°E).

similar_questions.stem: Eritrea is located between longitudes:
explanation_steps: Eritrea's longitudes are 36°E and 43°E. Answer: B.

questions.stem: The Turks occupied Massawa in:
explanation_steps: The textbook says: in 1557 the Turks occupied Massawa and Hirghigo (Social Studies Grade 6, p. 72; Grade 8, p. 64).
Answer: C.
questions.explain_simple: The Turks took Massawa in 1557.
tips: 1557 = Turks in Massawa.

similar_questions.stem: Which foreign power occupied Massawa in 1557?
explanation_steps: The Turks came in 1557. Answer: B.

explanation_steps: The textbook says: the capital of the Bahri Negastat was at Debarwa (Social Studies Grade 6, p. 69).
Answer: D.
questions.explain_simple: Debarwa was the capital of the Bahri Negestat.
tips: Bahri Negestat → capital Debarwa.

similar_questions.stem: The ruler of the Bahri Negestat was called:
explanation_steps: The ruler was the Bahri Negash. Answer: A.

questions.stem: 550 C.E is:
explanation_steps: The 6th century C.E. is the years 501 to 600 (Social Studies Grade 6, p. 13).
550 is in the middle of 501–600. Answer: B.
questions.explain_simple: 550 is in the middle of the years 501–600, the 6th century.
tips: To find the century: take the hundreds and add 1 (550 → 5 + 1 = 6th century).

similar_questions.stem: 1950 C.E. is in the middle of the:
explanation_steps: 1901–2000 is the 20th century; 1950 is its middle. Answer: B.

questions.stem: History is:

options.B: the story of kings and rulers
options.C: a description of wars and battles

explanation_steps: History is the study and record of past events (Social Studies Grade 6, p. 1).
It is about all people, not only kings or wars. Answer: A.
questions.explain_simple: History is the record of what happened in the past.
tips: History = past events of all people.

similar_questions.stem: Which of these is a written source of history?
explanation_steps: A letter is written. Answer: C.

questions.stem: A period of 10 years is called:
explanation_steps: A decade is a period of 10 years (Social Studies Grade 6, p. 9).
A century is 100 years and a millennium is 1000 years. Answer: C.
questions.explain_simple: 10 years = a decade.
tips: Decade 10, century 100, millennium 1000.

similar_questions.stem: A period of 100 years is called a:
explanation_steps: 100 years is a century. Answer: B.

questions.stem: 250 C.E is in the:
explanation_steps: The 3rd century C.E. is the years 201 to 300 (Social Studies Grade 6, p. 13).
250 is between 201 and 300. Answer: B.
questions.explain_simple: 250 is in the years 201–300, the third century.
tips: Hundreds + 1: 250 → 2 + 1 = 3rd century.

similar_questions.stem: The year 1420 C.E. is in the:
explanation_steps: 1401–1500 is the 15th century. Answer: B.

questions.stem: If the soils of an area are poor in mineral nutrients, then the area will be left for:
explanation_steps: The textbook says: soils poor in mineral nutrients are left for grazing animals (Social Studies Grade 6, p. 94).
Crops need good soil, so people use poor soil for grazing. Answer: B.
questions.explain_simple: Poor soil is used for grazing animals.
tips: Good soil → crops. Poor soil → grazing.

similar_questions.stem: Which area is best for growing crops?

options.A: An area with fertile soil and enough rain

explanation_steps: Crops grow well in fertile soil with rain. Answer: A.

questions.stem: The settlement of an area can be dispersed if:

options.B: the area is rich in minerals
options.D: there is more fish in that area

explanation_steps: Dispersed settlement means houses are far from each other.
In dry areas water and grass are scarce, so people and their animals spread out over a large area (Social Studies Grade 6, p. 37).
Minerals, fertile soil and fish attract many people to one place, so they give nucleated (close) settlements. Answer: A.
questions.explain_simple: In dry areas people live far from each other, so settlement is dispersed.
tips: Dispersed = scattered; nucleated = close together.

similar_questions.stem: Houses built close together in one place form a:
explanation_steps: Close houses make a nucleated settlement. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Social Studies Grade 6 textbook – Unit 6 – Settlement, 6.2 Types of settlement, p. 37
textbook_ref.subject: Social Studies

questions.stem: Mohammed and his family live by grazing animals. Their activity is an example of ______ economic activity.
explanation_steps: Primary activities take things directly from nature: farming, herding animals, fishing, mining (Social Studies Grade 6, pp. 95–96).
Grazing animals is herding, so it is primary. Answer: C.
questions.explain_simple: Keeping animals takes food from nature. It is a primary activity.
tips: Primary = from nature; secondary = making things; tertiary = services.

similar_questions.stem: A farmer who grows wheat does a ______ activity.
explanation_steps: Farming is primary. Answer: A.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Social Studies Grade 6 textbook – Unit 11 – Economic Activities, 11.2 Types of economic activities, p. 95-96
textbook_ref.subject: Social Studies

questions.stem: Adiam is a bus driver. Her activity is an example of _________ economic activity.
explanation_steps: Tertiary activities give services to people: transport, trade, teaching, health (Social Studies Grade 6, pp. 97–98).
A bus driver gives a transport service. Answer: B.
questions.explain_simple: A bus driver gives a service. It is a tertiary activity.
tips: Services (driver, teacher, doctor, shopkeeper) are tertiary.

similar_questions.stem: A worker in a shoe factory does a ______ activity.
explanation_steps: Making things in a factory is secondary. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Social Studies Grade 6 textbook – Unit 11 – Economic Activities, 11.2 Types of economic activities, p. 97-98
textbook_ref.subject: Social Studies

questions.stem: Which of these factors has <u>no</u> impact on the distribution of population?
explanation_steps: Population distribution depends on physical factors like climate, relief, soil and water, and on resources (Social Studies Grade 7, Unit 2.2).
Composition (age and sex groups) describes the population. It does not decide where people live. Answer: C.
questions.explain_simple: Climate, relief and resources decide where people live. Composition does not.
tips: Composition = age and sex of people. Distribution = where people live.

similar_questions.stem: Why do few people live in very hot deserts?

options.D: There is a lot of water

explanation_steps: A harsh climate keeps people away. Answer: A.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Social Studies Grade 7 textbook – Unit 2 – Population, 2.2 B. Factors of Population Distribution, p. 17-18

questions.stem: One of the following decreases the amount of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere:

options.B: an increase in use of fossil fuels
options.C: an increase in use of fire wood

explanation_steps: Plants take in carbon dioxide and give out oxygen (Social Studies Grade 6, p. 82).
More forests take more carbon dioxide out of the air. Burning fuel or wood and cutting forests add carbon dioxide (Grade 7, p. 34). Answer: D.
questions.explain_simple: Trees take in carbon dioxide. More trees mean less carbon dioxide.
tips: Burning adds CO₂; planting trees removes CO₂.

similar_questions.stem: Which activity adds carbon dioxide to the air?
explanation_steps: Burning charcoal releases carbon dioxide. Answer: B.

questions.stem: Which of these is a result of global warming?

options.C: melting of the polar ice caps

explanation_steps: Burning fuels and deforestation are causes of global warming.
The textbook lists the melting of the polar ice caps as a result (Social Studies Grade 7, p. 35). Answer: C.
questions.explain_simple: Global warming melts the ice at the poles.
tips: Cause = what makes it happen; result = what happens after.

similar_questions.stem: Which is a cause of global warming?
explanation_steps: Burning fossil fuels causes global warming. Answer: C.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Social Studies Grade 7 textbook – Unit 3 – People and the Environment, 3.2 Global warming, p. 34-35

questions.stem: One of the following is <u>not</u> a reason for the decrease of the number of wild animals in Eritrea.
explanation_steps: Wild animals decreased because of drought, war, hunting and the loss of their homes when farms expanded (Social Studies Grade 7, 7.4).
Tourism is not given as a reason; well-planned tourism can help protect wildlife. Answer: A.
questions.explain_simple: Farms, drought and war reduced wild animals. Tourism did not.
tips: Loss of habitat (home) is a main reason animals disappear.

similar_questions.stem: Which of these helps to protect wild animals?
explanation_steps: Protected areas keep animals safe. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Social Studies Grade 7 textbook – Unit 7 – Natural Heritages, 7.4 Terrestrial (Land) Vegetation and Wild Animals, p. 106-107
textbook_ref.subject: Social Studies

questions.stem: Domestication of animals means:

options.B: keeping and using cattle for human benefit
options.C: keeping wild animals away from cattle

explanation_steps: Early people kept some animals near them and used them. This led to cattle breeding, called domestication of animals (Social Studies Grade 7, p. 65).
Answer: B.
questions.explain_simple: Domestication means keeping animals and using them.
tips: Domestic animals = animals living with people (cows, goats, camels).

similar_questions.stem: Which one is a domestic animal?
explanation_steps: Goats are kept by people. Answer: B.

questions.stem: Tribes were:
explanation_steps: The textbook says: clans joined together to form tribes (Social Studies Grade 7, p. 79).
Answer: A.
questions.explain_simple: A tribe is a group of clans.
tips: Family → clan → tribe.

similar_questions.stem: A group of related families is called a:
explanation_steps: Related families form a clan. Answer: A.

questions.stem: Which of the following is <u>not</u> a branch of government?
explanation_steps: The three branches of government are the legislature, the judiciary and the executive (Social Studies Grade 7, p. 85).
Federalism is a system of government, not a branch. Answer: B.
questions.explain_simple: Federalism is not a branch of government.
tips: Three branches: make laws, carry out laws, judge.

similar_questions.stem: Which branch of government makes laws?
explanation_steps: The legislature makes laws. Answer: C.

questions.stem: In Eritrea the highest point is about 3000 meters above sea level and the lowest point is about 100 meters below sea level. Then the difference between the highest and the lowest points is about:
explanation_steps: Below sea level is like a negative number: −100 m.
(The textbook gives about 120 m below sea level to over 3000 m, Social Studies Grade 8, p. 2.)
questions.explain_simple: Add the height above and the depth below sea level: 3000 + 100 = 3100 m.
tips: One point above and one below sea level: add them.

questions.stem: Which one is part of underground water?
explanation_steps: Underground (ground) water is water under the surface of the earth. The textbook says: the water in springs and wells comes from ground water (Social Studies Grade 8, p. 12).
Rivers, seas and dams are surface water. Answer: C.
questions.explain_simple: A well takes water from under the ground.
tips: Surface water: rivers, lakes, dams, seas. Ground water: wells, springs.

similar_questions.stem: Which of these is surface water?
explanation_steps: A lake is on the surface. Answer: C.

questions.stem: A river is permanent if:

options.C: there is rain throughout the year
options.D: the rainfall is high but seasonal

explanation_steps: Rivers in areas that get rain throughout the year are permanent rivers; their water is high (Social Studies Grade 8, p. 16).
Seasonal rain gives seasonal rivers. Answer: C.
questions.explain_simple: A river always has water if it rains all year.
tips: Rain all year → permanent river. Rain in one season → seasonal river.

similar_questions.stem: Most rivers in Eritrea are:
explanation_steps: Eritrea gets seasonal rain, so most rivers are seasonal. Answer: B.

questions.stem: The conflict between the Portuguese and the Turks was caused:

options.A: by their desire to control the region of the Horn
options.B: because of the alliance of the Abyssinian king and the Turks
options.C: because both wanted to control the trade with the East

explanation_steps: The textbook says both the Turks and the Portuguese were expanding their power in the region and wanted to control the Red Sea trade with the East (Social Studies Grade 6, pp. 73–74).
So both A and C are reasons. B is wrong: the Abyssinian king allied with the Portuguese, not the Turks. Answer: D.
questions.explain_simple: Both wanted power in the Horn and control of trade. So A and C.
tips: Check each statement before choosing 'A and C'.

similar_questions.stem: Who did the Abyssinian king ask for help against Gragn?
explanation_steps: He asked the Portuguese. Answer: B.

questions.stem: Which of the following followed expansionist policies in Eritrea ?
explanation_steps: The textbook says: from the 16th to the 19th centuries the Turks, Abyssinians, Egyptians and Italians tried to establish themselves in Eritrea (Social Studies Grade 8, p. 63).
Tigrean rulers (like Ras Alula) also attacked Eritrea. So both A and B are correct. Answer: D.
questions.explain_simple: Tigrean/Abyssinian rulers, Egyptians and Turks all tried to take Eritrea.
tips: Remember the invaders: Turks, Abyssinians (Tigreans), Egyptians, Italians.

similar_questions.stem: Which power was defeated at the battles of Gundet and Gura?
explanation_steps: The Egyptians were defeated there. Answer: B.

questions.stem: Which of the following is <u>true</u> about Mahber Fikri Hager?

options.B: It defended the needs of the Italians
options.C: It was an association opposed to colonialism

explanation_steps: The textbook says: in 1941 a movement called Mahber Fiqri Hager was formed. It was an anti-colonial association (Social Studies Grade 8, p. 81). So C is true.
History books give the founding date as 5 May 1941, so A is also true. The textbook gives only the year 1941.
It worked for the needs of Eritreans, not Italians, so B is false. Answer: D.
questions.explain_simple: It was founded in 1941 and it was against colonialism. So A and C.
tips: Mahber Fikri Hager (1941) = love of country, against colonialism.

similar_questions.stem: Mahber Fikri Hager was formed during the rule of the:
explanation_steps: It was formed in 1941, when the British replaced the Italians. Answer: B.

questions.review_flag: The textbook (G8 p. 81) gives only the year 1941, not the exact date 'May 5, 1941' in option A. Answer D depends on this date, which is not in the textbook (it is the date usually given in history books). If a teacher does not accept A, then C alone is correct.

questions.stem: Which of the following pairs does <u>not</u> match?
explanation_steps: Under Italian rule, the commissari (commissioners) were Italian officials who ran the regions (Social Studies Grade 8, p. 92 area, Unit 6).
Eritreans served as bandas (irregular soldiers) and zaptias (police). Italian rule had racist laws. So C does not match. Answer: C.
questions.explain_simple: The commissari were Italians, not Eritreans.
tips: Italian rule: Italians were commissari; Eritreans were askaris, bandas and zaptias.

similar_questions.stem: Eritrean soldiers in the Italian colonial army were called:
explanation_steps: They were called askaris. Answer: A.

questions.stem: Deggiat Hailu of Tseazzega was defeated by Ras Woldemichael at the Battle of:
explanation_steps: The textbook tells that Ras Woldemichael defeated Deggiat Hailu of Tseazzega at the Battle of Wokki Duba (Social Studies Grade 8, pp. 72–73).
Answer: D.
questions.explain_simple: The battle was at Wokki Duba.
tips: Make a table of battles: who fought, who won, the year.

similar_questions.stem: Where did the Egyptians suffer their final defeat?
explanation_steps: Their final defeat was at Gura (1876). Answer: B.

questions.stem: Which of the following <u>does not</u> improve soil fertility?
explanation_steps: Soil fertility is kept by crop rotation, fallowing (resting the land) and terracing (which stops soil from washing away) (Social Studies Grade 6, p. 84).
Over cultivation uses the soil too much and makes it poor. Answer: B.
questions.explain_simple: Using the land too much makes the soil poor.
tips: 'Over-' words (overgrazing, over cultivation) are bad for the land.

similar_questions.stem: Leaving land without crops for a season to rest is called:
explanation_steps: Resting land is fallowing. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Social Studies Grade 6 textbook – Unit 10 – Natural Resources and Conservation, 10.2 Soil, p. 84

questions.stem: Eritrea was federated with Ethiopia by:
explanation_steps: On 2 December 1950 the UN passed Resolution 390A(V), which federated Eritrea with Ethiopia (Social Studies Grade 8, p. 83).
Answer: C.
questions.explain_simple: UN Resolution 390A(V) joined Eritrea to Ethiopia in a federation.
tips: 390A(V): passed 1950, federation started 1952.

explanation_steps: It started in September 1952. Answer: B.

questions.explain_simple: The Egyptians were finally defeated at Gura (1876).
tips: Gundet 1875 → Gura 1876 (end of Egyptian push).

similar_questions.stem: The Battle of Dogali (1887) was fought against the:

questions.stem: In Eritrea fishing is:

options.A: the main economic activity of the island population
options.B: the main source of export income
options.C: the main source of food for the majority of the people

explanation_steps: The textbook says: the main economic activity of the people of the coastal areas and islands, especially south of Massawa, is fishing (Social Studies Grade 8, p. 140).
Fish is an export, but not the main source of export income, and most Eritreans live on farming. Answer: A.
questions.explain_simple: People on the islands live mainly by fishing.
tips: Coast and islands → fishing; highlands → farming.

similar_questions.stem: The largest island group of Eritrea is:
explanation_steps: The Dahlak archipelago is the largest. Answer: A.

explanation_steps: Maize, millet and wheat are cereals (grains).
Sesame is an oil seed (Social Studies Grade 8, p. 131 area). Answer: B.
questions.explain_simple: Sesame gives oil. The others are cereals.
tips: Cereals: wheat, barley, maize, sorghum, millet, taff. Oil seeds: sesame, linseed, groundnut.

similar_questions.stem: Which one is an oil seed?
explanation_steps: Groundnut is an oil seed. Answer: C.

Dogali was in 1887, Eritrea was declared an Italian colony in 1890, and Ethiopia annexed Eritrea in 1962.
The earliest is 1869. Answer: B.
questions.explain_simple: Sapeto bought Assab in 1869. That is the earliest.
tips: Write the year next to each event, then order them.

questions.explain_simple: Liberation in 1991 came after all the others.

Pottery, basketry and goldsmith work are traditional handicrafts. Answer: A.
questions.explain_simple: A textile factory uses machines. It is a modern industry.
tips: Factory + machines = modern. Hand work = traditional (cottage) industry.

similar_questions.stem: Which of these is a traditional (cottage) industry?
explanation_steps: Basket making is done by hand. Answer: B.

tips: Years ÷ 10 = decades.

similar_questions.stem: How many decades are there from 1950 to 2010?
explanation_steps: 2010 − 1950 = 60 years = 6 decades. Answer: C.

questions.stem: Figure 1 below shows the map of an area. If the map distance between town A and town B along the road is 15cm find the ground distance between the two towns in kilometers. Scale: 1cm to 2km.
questions.image_alt: Map with Town A (bottom left) and Town B (top right) joined by a curved road. Scale: 1 cm to 2 km.
explanation_steps: The scale says 1 cm on the map = 2 km on the ground.
Ground distance = map distance × scale = 15 × 2 km = 30 km (Social Studies Grade 6, pp. 16–20). Answer: D.
questions.explain_simple: Each 1 cm is 2 km, so 15 cm is 30 km.
tips: Ground distance = map distance × the ground value of 1 cm.

similar_questions.stem: On a map, 1 cm stands for 5 km. Two towns are 8 cm apart on the map. The real distance is:
explanation_steps: 8 × 5 = 40 km. Answer: B.

questions.stem: The struggle between the Bahri Negassi and the Turks was caused by

options.A: Friendship of the Turks with the Abyssinian kings
options.B: Turkish desire to control the Red Sea trade routes
options.C: Friendship of the Portuguese and the Turks

explanation_steps: The Turks wanted to control the Red Sea and its trade routes, so they occupied Massawa and Hirghigo (Social Studies Grade 6, pp. 72–73).
The Turks were not friends of the Abyssinian kings or the Portuguese; they were rivals. Answer: B.
questions.explain_simple: The Turks wanted to control the Red Sea trade.
tips: Turks and Portuguese were enemies, not friends.

similar_questions.stem: Which Bahri Negash fought against the Turks?
explanation_steps: Bahri Negash Yeshaq fought the Turks. Answer: A.

questions.stem: The length of a classroom is 12 meters and its width is 8 meters. Figure 2 below shows the floor plan (floor map) drawn using a scale. What is the scale of the plan (map)?
questions.image_alt: Figure 2: a rectangle 6 cm long and 4 cm wide (floor plan of the classroom).
explanation_steps: On the plan the length is 6 cm and the real length is 12 m. So 6 cm = 12 m, and 1 cm = 2 m.
Check the width: 4 cm × 2 m = 8 m. Correct. Answer: C.
questions.explain_simple: 6 cm stands for 12 m, so 1 cm stands for 2 m.
tips: Scale: divide the real length by the plan length.

similar_questions.stem: A field 100 m long is drawn 10 cm long on a plan. The scale is:
explanation_steps: 100 ÷ 10 = 10, so 1 cm to 10 m. Answer: A.

questions.stem: Which of these statements is <u>correct</u>?

options.A: Most of the work in the primitive Communal System was done by slaves
options.B: Differences in wealth caused the appearance of classes
options.C: In Slave Society priests and nobles were the lowest class
options.D: Settled communities appeared before crop production

explanation_steps: The textbook says: differences in wealth led to the appearance of classes (Social Studies Grade 7, p. 71). So B is correct.
A is wrong (there were no slaves or classes in primitive communal society). C is wrong (slaves were the lowest class). D is wrong (crop production came first, then people settled).
questions.explain_simple: Classes appeared because some people became richer than others.
tips: Primitive communal = no classes; slave society = first class society.

similar_questions.stem: The first society with classes was the:
explanation_steps: Slave society was the first class society. Answer: B.

questions.image_alt: Four drawings of the water cycle. 1: wavy arrows rise from a water surface. 2: wavy arrows rise from trees and plants. 3: a cloud with arrows (rain) falling down. 4: rivers flowing into the sea.

Drawing 1 shows vapour rising from water. Answer: D.
questions.explain_simple: Drawing 1 shows water going up from the water surface.
tips: Evaporation: from water. Transpiration: from plants. Precipitation: falling rain.

similar_questions.stem: Water vapour cooling into clouds is called:
explanation_steps: Vapour becomes cloud by condensation. Answer: B.

passages.title: Figure 3 – The water cycle (Questions 48 to 50)
passages.instructions: In Figure 3, drawings 1, 2, 3, and 4 show different parts of the water cycle. Answer questions 48 to 50 based on the information given.
paragraphs: Figure 3 has four drawings. Drawing 1: wavy arrows go up from the surface of water. Drawing 2: wavy arrows go up from trees and plants. Drawing 3: a cloud with arrows (rain) coming down. Drawing 4: rivers flowing into a large body of water (the sea).
